title: pub struct MemoryBackend lacks #[non_exhaustive] — future field additions are SemVer breaking
description:
Location: crate-jmap-filenode-server/src/memory.rs:165-168

```rust
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct MemoryBackend {
    inner: Arc<Mutex<MemoryState>>,
}
```

`#[non_exhaustive]` is missing. The single field is private so
struct-literal construction is already blocked from outside the
crate, but `#[non_exhaustive]` is the documented signal of
forward-compatibility intent in Rust public types. Without it, a
linter or human reviewer cannot tell at-a-glance whether the type
is locked or evolvable.

Adding a field like `config: MemoryConfig` (for the bd:JMAP-510h.16
configurable rename-suffix cap) or
`max_change_log_entries: Option<usize>` (for the "change log grows
without bound" issue in the canonical sibling docstring) is
SemVer-safe right now because the field is private, but the annotation
makes that intent explicit and survives a future refactor where
someone adds a `pub` field.

Propagation note: canonical sibling
`crate-jmap-mail-server/src/memory.rs:251` (also a private-field
struct) has the same omission. Both should land the annotation in
the same pass — mail-server canonical first.

This is `api-contract,immutability` because the convention for the
workspace ("`#[non_exhaustive]` on every public struct" — per the
crate-jmap AGENTS.md "Key Rules" and "Conventions & Patterns" lists)
is missed here. The repair is mechanical and the cost is one line
per struct.
